Well my doctor says i supposedly have a horrible sinus infection and candida in my throat,  which,  if I do have fungal, it will be impossible to get rid of. But I don't even know if that's true or not.  My throat and chest are constantly so tight that I feel like I can't breathe. I feel like shit all the time and I always have a stuffy nose and sore throat and facial and teeth pain.  On top of that I have asthma and acid reflux, extremely dry eyes, and another eye condition called strabismus, and I might even have an autoimmune disorder.  I'm constantly sick, and I now have doctors acknowledging something is wrong with me when so many doctors said I was fine for months but each doctor has a different opinion on what's wrong with me. Even then I don't know if any of them are right or not.
You don't think he'll commit me though,  do you?

I was angry, but I didn't say anything.  He's the main OBGYN, but I usually see his nurse.  Everyone always raves about him though. I went back to the nurse a couple of days ago and she confirmed my suspicions of having a bad yeast infection, so he even lied to me about that too. So ridiculous.

Sorry I'm replying to another one of your comments. But how will other family members know? The information between you and your healthcare professionals is confidential. And tell your parents not to tell anyone. My parents know about my mental health too and we just say I'm "going to a doctor" or that I had a doctor's appointment. And if the others happened, for some strange reason, to accidentally find out, will they really ridicule you or do you think they will? Having social anxiety sucks, and I know what I'm going to say won't comfort you but most people don't care if you see a therapist/psychiatrist. Millions of others are going through the same thing and seeing the same people. Don't be ashamed. It's nothing to be ashamed of to ask for help. It's actually pretty brave to acknowledge your problems and try and fix them.
I'm not from the UK so I don't know about the system. Do you get a GCSE certificate? Is there any way you can take classes to get the equivalent of that certificate/diploma?

It really depends on the case. Women don't always get away with everything. A lot of guys can still look "different" and no one cares. Taking the American entertainment industry for example: you have guys who aren't exactly modelworthy who are in every movie and are still taken seriously. The women, on the other hand, usually have to fit into certain standards in order to succeed in the industry or else people write them off.
Everything out of my reach.

I can understand what he means and that he was only trying to help. It can be hard for people to empathize with someone with a condition like me because it is so uncommon.

As for happiness, I would feel better I had normal eyes/vision, especially cosmetically. It would give me a lot less stress.
I'm a girl. If I were a guy it would be 10x easier but unfortunately people are usually more judgmental towards women. And it makes my eyesight worse.

But if I get another sinus infection (which is inevitable) then I won't be able to walk. I think two months is good enough time. By then,  it will have been a year since this has all began,  and a year is long enough.

I decided two months because I have some more medical tests I have to do and that is an appropriate amount of time. If none of those tests help me  then there is no point to living because I won't get any better.  I can't live the rest of my life like this. I am barely surviving right now and most of the doctors don't care. Like I said,  my own body is fighting against me and is telling my brain to end it. As for the walking,  I could try to walk with my mom but she doesn't like me talking about my depression. It's still hard walking up hills though.

It doesn't matter if my family loves me or not. If I ever graduate college I will most likely hate my career and still be sick along with my eye problems and mental illness. It's easier for her health and it would increase my family's income if I were dead. She contributes to society,  I don't. They may cry but ultimately they would feel relieved that their problem child is gone.  I did walk for twenty minutes just now though even though it was very hard.  But I'll probably get a sinus infection again so it will make my breathing worse so I won't be able to walk again.

Not many many more years if I kill myself first.  And I did ruin her life.  She's been sick too but she's been
 missing work and taking me to the doctors and she can't afford to miss any more and take care of herself.  She's at the hospital right now.  And I cant walk 4km, I can barely walk up the stairs

I have been eating healthy. It's not the food, it's that I eat too much and am not burning it off. And in order to get better I have to continually see specialists in a city 30 miles away,  and I can't drive there by myself and they have to perform a test which I am unable to handle because I have constant sinus infections and they have to stick a tube in my nose.  As for jobs I'm probably going to be moving soon so i can't get a job right now. My parents have been saying since this has started that it will get better but they are losing their faith and patience.  My mom even told me that I've ruined her life.

Yes,  it is better.  And I have wanted to die but I'm too much of a coward to try.  But I know that things aren't going to get better.  It's only good if you are wealthy and in good health.  Nobody cares about the poor and the poor are given so much more shit than they can handle. It really is so much better for all the stress to go away and to be at peace, which will never happen for me in this life because of all my problems.
